svg.text: COPPER SIDE, mirrored: what you see when you cut the tracks
53 × 22 holes · cut to 134.6 × 55.9 mm · 23 cuts · 16 links · 2 standoff holes (2.5 mm, for M2.5 nylon standoffs)
Drive XLR L balanced: hot follows HPL, cold is its inverse, +8.2 dBu at full scale; −20 dB on Mic; muted until the pedal is ready.
C17 47µF 63V bipolar — 63 V bipolar: pair it with C18 on a meter, within 5
C18 47µF 63V bipolar — 63 V bipolar: the pair of C17
D7 1N4148 — across the coil, band towards +5 V
D8 1N5817 — band on the top rail (9 V filtered)
D10 1N5817 — band on the bottom rail (9 V filtered)
K2 TQ2-5V — stripe to the top. Both poles mute in parallel: COM to X, NC to
R32 10k 0.1% — 0.1 %: sets how equal hot and cold are
R34 100Ω 1% — 1 %: hot and cold must match, so R34 = R35 and R41 = R42
R41 10Ω 1% — limits a charged C17 shorting through the clamps (3.7 A, not
U5 OPA2197 — OPA2197 on its SOIC adapter, in an 8-pin socket. Pin 1 at the
Connectors (pin 1 is the large filled square)
A11 → Codec carrier, JST-XH 5-way (B5B-XH-A): 1 GND · 2 HPL · 3 GND · 4 +9
A15 → XLR L out, JST-XH 3-way (B3B-XH-A): 1 LINE · 2 COM · 3 MIC
No ground: a toggle: three signal wires.
C7 → Control: Pico 2 WH, JST-XH 3-way (B3B-XH-A): 1 COIL − · 2 — · 3 +5 V
No ground: as C1: the coil’s low side is switched on the control board.
A13 → XLR L out, JST-XH 2-way (B2B-XH-A): 1 HOT · 2 COLD
No ground: pin 1 goes to the case through the lift toggle, so no ground
reaches the driver from the XLR.
GND reaches the root through A11 only (Codec carrier).
Build it twice; L and R are identical and swap. The schematic, its wiring
table and the simulation are schematic/balanced-output/,
Ground arrives on the input cable from the codec carrier, with the signal
and the 9 V, and that is this board’s only ground. Pin 1 of the XLR is the
case’s, through the lift toggle: the XLR cable brings no ground here.
The mute relay de-energised shorts X to VREF. Its coil is wired in parallel
with the bypass relay’s, so the XLR is silent at boot, in panic bypass and
on any failure. Confirm its contacts with a meter as for the bypass relay:
pin 4 to pin 2 and pin 7 to pin 9 should beep with the coil unpowered.
The pad and coil plugs are both three-way. Swapped, neither harms anything
(the toggle would only work the relay), but label them.

Red ✕: cut the track at that hole (red bar: cut between two holes). Lines: wire links on the component side (green carries ground). Strips tinted green carry ground, red a supply, amber 3.3 V. White circles: standoff holes; dashed: what the standoff covers.
